candidate.answerReason: On the stated domain, (sec x-tan x)(sec x+tan x)=1. Since the first factor is 2, the requested factor is 1/2.

methods.label: Multiply the sum and difference
methods.explanation:
The given difference and the requested sum form a difference-of-squares product. Since \(\sec x\) and \(\tan x\) are defined, \(\cos x\ne0\). Using \(\sec x=1/\cos x\), \(\tan x=\sin x/\cos x\), and \(\sin^2x+\cos^2x=1\), we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
(\sec x-\tan x)(\sec x+\tan x)
&=\sec^2x-\tan^2x\\
&=\frac{1-\sin^2x}{\cos^2x}\\
&=1.
\end{aligned}
\]
Substituting the given value yields \(2(\sec x+\tan x)=1\). Dividing by the nonzero number \(2\),
\[
\sec x+\tan x=\frac12=0.5.
\]
The answer is choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
